discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 190721
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
221 AM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Above normal temperatures continue through Sunday.

- Dry for the rest of the work week. Then, chances for rain 
  increase later Saturday night into Sunday night (40-60%)

- A normal to slightly below normal temperature period takes
  over for next week and the forecast leans dry through at least
  Tuesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 208 AM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

A deep area of subsidence sits across the Mid Atlantic region and 
stretches into the Lower Great Lakes. One trough was able to ride 
along its northwest side and into Canada, but our local area will 
continue to be dry today through at least Saturday as the 
surface high pressure area combines with the mid level ridging 
to provide dry air. With the dry air, today, it will be possible
to generate low level lapse rates quick enough to produce gusty
winds to 20 to 30 mph, especially if mixing takes hold. 
However, there are some models that have some low level moisture
that intrudes on these rates. Therefore, the gusts are 
possible, but come with lower confidence.

Now, by the time we get to Friday night, the surface high pressure 
area and mid level ridging are being impinged on by the large mid 
level trough pushing through the Western US. A fairly vigorous 
shortwave is able to dig down into Texas and make its way towards 
the area Sunday. The issue is that it's dampening out by the time it 
gets here and it's pretty quick through the area. A delayed arrival 
closer to the GFS depiction could mean more instability gets to the 
area, but the thin line of moisture could prevent any local impacts 
from rain and potential storms even if it has 1 to 2 SDs above 
normal PWATs. 

Surface high pressure takes over for Monday and this allows for a 
return to dry air. Cold air also pushes into the area, and 
while our lows were in the 30s and 40s this morning, they'll be
able to drop down into the mid to upper 20s Monday night. We 
recently had this magnitude of cold air to start the day between
11/14 and 11/17. These cold morning temps are expected to stay 
with us through the end of next week. This is as our highs 
flatten out around 40 degrees next week after Monday. One 
interesting aspect about Monday and Tuesday is that with the 
cold air filtering in, 850 mb temps cool below zero bottoming 
out around -9 or -10C Monday night. This produces a Delta T 
around -15 to -20C so this is probably more of a lake effect 
cloud scenario than a widespread lake effect rain event.

Beyond this point, different model handling of a wave moving through 
the Central Plains provides less confidence on main forcing between 
whether it stays south along the Gulf States within the subtropical 
jet or within the Pacific Jet across the Northern Tier of the US. 
Despite their differences in forcing, though, the GFS and ECMWF are 
both consistent in keeping precipitation out of the area for the end 
of the work week.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 1257 AM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

VFR conditions are expected at both terminals, with winds
strengthening out of the south-southwest this afternoon,
especially at KSBN where gusts up to around 20 knots are
possible.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

spc.text:
SPC AC 190547

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1147 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

   Valid 191200Z - 201200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   CENTRAL CALIFORNIA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts and perhaps a brief
   tornado are possible today in central California, from the San
   Joaquin Valley westward to near San Francisco.

   ...Central California...
   An upper-level low will move eastward today across the southwestern
   part of the Pacific Northwest. The associated trough will move
   across central and northern California. At the surface, a low will
   move into the Sierra Nevada as a cold front advances southward
   across northern California. Weak instability will develop ahead of
   the front over much of central California, where SBCAPE is expected
   to peak near 500 J/kg this afternoon. As a band of strong
   large-ascent associated with the trough moves through central
   California, scattered thunderstorm development will become likely.
   RAP forecast soundings at 21Z ahead of this band of ascent have 0-6
   km shear in the 30 to 40 knot range with 700-500 mb lapse rates
   around 7.5 C/km. This environment along with the instability will
   support an isolated severe threat during the afternoon. A few severe
   wind gusts will be possible, along with potential for a brief
   tornado.

   ..Broyles/Chalmers.. 11/19/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 190700

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0100 AM CST Thu Nov 19 2026

   Valid 201200Z - 211200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms do not appear likely Friday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A broad upper trough over the Southwest is forecast to approach and
   eventually cross the Rockies Friday into early Saturday. The primary
   vort max will slow over the Four Corners as a weaker embedded
   perturbation rapidly lifts northeastward across the Plains and upper
   Midwest. At the surface, a lee cyclone will bifurcate as one lobe
   lifts away with the shortwave trough over the northern Plains.
   Behind this low, a cold front will sweep eastward across the Dakotas
   while trailing back to the second weaker low over western NE and
   eastern CO. A nebulous upper trough will be present over parts of
   the Southeast into the Gulf. A modest surface low will be present
   off the central Florida Atlantic coast.

   ...Central/Northern Plains...
   As the upper trough move into the Plains, southerly flow will assist
   modest surface moisture return ahead of the primary surface low and
   advancing cold front. Likely limited in quality owing to the rapid
   return, low 50s F dewpoints reaching the central/northern Plains is
   a plausible upper-end outcome by Friday evening. Steepening
   mid-level lapse rates and strong ascent will help develop weak
   buoyancy along the cold front by late afternoon into the evening.
   Isolated storm development is possible across NE and southern SD
   near the front most likely after 00Z. Given the limited moisture and
   generally cool surface temperatures, this activity would likely be
   somewhat elevated. Severe potential is unlikely given the weak
   instability.

   ...FL...
   Attendant to the broad and weak upper trough over the eastern Gulf,
   subtle convergence along typical sea breeze boundaries and the
   developing surface low should support scattered to numerous
   thunderstorms Friday and Friday night across FL. Buoyancy, mid-level
   lapse rates and vertical shear should remain modest limiting the
   potential for more organized/stronger storms.

   ..Lyons.. 11/19/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 190830

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0230 AM CST Thu Nov 19 2026

   Valid 211200Z - 221200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS
   OF NORTH TEXAS OKLAHOMA AND KANSAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe storms are possible over the central and
   southern Plains Saturday.

   ...Central and Southern Plains...
   A diffuse upper trough with several embedded perturbations will move
   eastward from the Rockies into the Plains Saturday. The primary vort
   max over the Four Corners will eject over the southern Plains with a
   belt of 50+ kt southwesterly flow aloft. At the surface, a cold
   front will extend from the Canadian border, across the central
   Plains to a lee cyclone over southeastern CO and the western OK/TX
   Panhandles with a surface trough/weak dryline to the south over the
   southern High Plains. The surface low is forecast to deepen modestly
   through the day, drawing 50s to perhaps near 60 F surface dewpoints
   northward as it and the front move eastward.

   Model forecast soundings show generally poor lapse rates across much
   of the warm sector likely owing to lingering cloud cover from the
   rapid low-level warm advection. This should mute overall buoyancy
   with most guidance showing MLCAPE of 250-500 J/kg over the southern
   Plains and likely less farther north. Sufficient buoyancy and the
   increase in forcing for ascent should allow for scattered
   thunderstorms to develop along and behind the front from KS/MO into
   OK/TX in the afternoon. Deep-layer bulk shear values of 40-50 kt
   could support some stronger storms capable of isolated hail or
   damaging wind gusts. Additional storms, mostly behind the front, may
   develop after dark as the front surge southeastward.

   ...Southeast Atlantic Coast...
   A surface cyclone, possibly subtropical in nature, is forecast to
   deepen Saturday off the Atlantic coast. Appreciable boundary-layer
   moisture is likely to stay mostly offshore, but a few thunderstorms
   are possible along the Outer Banks into early Sunday. Severe storms
   are not expected here.

   ..Lyons.. 11/19/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
